writeup.headline: Allient rates Hold: solid growth and strong momentum offset by a high valuation and a leveraged balance sheet.
writeup.thesis: Allient scores 48, a Hold that sits just 4 points above the Sell line. Growth is a support, with TTM revenue growth of 10.6% and growth sped up by 5.6 pp from the previous quarter, and the trend score of 75 reflects shares up 107.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago. Valuation is the main drag (score 20). In absolute terms the multiples are high, with P/FCF of 59.5x, EV/EBIT of 36.5x and an FCF yield 3.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock is expensive against its own history. The balance sheet scores only 30, with net debt at 4.77 times FCF and cash covering 0.24 of debt, while quality is middling: an 8.4% operating margin and a 4.8% FCF margin.
key_risks: Valuation is high in absolute terms and more expensive than at 59 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S and EV/EBIT, leaving little room for disappointment.
Leverage is meaningful, with net debt at 4.77 times FCF and cash-to-debt of 0.24.
Analyst sentiment has cooled: JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral on valuation and Zacks cut to Hold.
Momentum may be fading, with the price 4.1% below its 50-day average and 18.9% below its 52-week high.
Thin FCF margin of 4.8% means modest cash generation relative to the share price.
what_would_change: A drop of 4 points in the score would move the rating to Sell, for example from weaker trend or a disappointing Q3 FY2026 report on November 4.
Reaching Buy needs 17 more points, most plausibly from a better valuation score through a lower share price or much higher free cash flow.
Reducing debt so net debt to FCF falls would lift the balance sheet score.
Continued revenue acceleration with margin expansion would raise the growth and quality scores.
